objective_for_doctor: A 63-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have haunting pain, a knife stroke pain, and tugging pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have very bad head pain—like a knife-stroke, tugging, and haunting pain. It’s sharp and violent, mostly in my forehead, my left cheek, and my right temple, and it came on really fast. My pain is about 7 out of 10.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—before I decide what this is, I need a few quick details: does the pain feel like a new, sudden “worst-ever” headache, and have you had any vision changes (blurred/double vision), weakness/numbness, fever, stiff neck, or fainting? Also, how long has it been going on since it started?

It was sudden and came on really fast, like a worst-ever kind of pain. I don’t have any vision changes, weakness or numbness, fever, stiff neck, or fainting. It started very quickly and has been going on since then.

Doctor: Given it’s a sudden “worst-ever” headache without fever/neck stiffness or neuro deficits, I’m concerned about dangerous causes like subarachnoid hemorrhage or temporal arteritis; can you tell me your age and whether you have scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, or recent vision loss? Also, do you have nausea/vomiting or light sensitivity?

Doctor: I need to rule out hemorrhage urgently—REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW.
I’m 63. I don’t have jaw pain when chewing or recent vision loss, and I don’t think I have scalp tenderness. I don’t have nausea/vomiting or light sensitivity.

Doctor: Thanks—since you’re 63 with sudden severe “worst-ever” facial/temple pain and no jaw claudication/vision loss, the next critical step is to check the blood-work/temporal-artery inflammation; REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP.  
Doctor: Also, to look for vascular causes or nerve-related causes when CT is negative, do you have any pain triggered by touch to the face, chewing, or brushing your teeth?
I don’t have pain triggered by touch to my face, chewing, or brushing my teeth. I also don’t have jaw pain with chewing.

Doctor: With sudden onset “worst-ever” unilateral forehead/temple/cheek pain at 63, no neuro deficits, no fever, no jaw claudication, and no touch/chewing trigger, I’m still worried about a vascular emergency even if ESR/CRP are normal—REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiography_Head_and_Neck.  
Doctor: While that’s pending, I need one more key question: do you have any tearing/red eye on the painful side or nasal congestion/runny nose with the attacks?  
Doctor: If you don’t, my working diagnosis shifts toward trigeminal autonomic-type headache vs other secondary causes once imaging is back.
No, I don’t have tearing or a red eye on the painful side, and I don’t have nasal congestion or a runny nose with the attacks.

Doctor: Given sudden “worst-ever” onset at 63 with facial/temple distribution and no autonomic symptoms (no tearing/red eye, no congestion), once CT/CTA and ESR/CRP return, the remaining top cause to consider is a secondary headache—especially vascular (e.g., small bleed/ischemia not seen early) versus trigeminal autonomic headache. REQUEST TEST: Results_of_Requested_CT/CTA_and_ESR_CRP.  

Doctor: While we await those results, are you able to rate whether the pain is strictly one-sided only, and does it worsen with movement/straining (cough, bending, straining)?
I think it’s strictly on one side—my left cheek and right temple/forehead area feel like the main spots. It doesn’t get worse when I move, cough, bend, or strain.

Doctor: Thank you—one-sided, severe sudden facial/temple pain at 63 without triggers, fever, neuro deficits, or autonomic symptoms makes trigeminal autonomic headache less likely but a secondary vascular/intracranial cause still must be excluded; REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_MRA_or_CT_MRV_if_needed.  
Doctor: If imaging is negative, the most likely diagnosis would be a primary neuralgiform disorder/cluster-spectrum—but I need the CT/CTA + ESR/CRP results to be safe; please share those results now.
I don’t have the results yet—tests like CT/CTA, ESR/CRP, or MRI haven’t been done or reported to me in this moment.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as a potential emergency until proven otherwise—because your pain was sudden and “worst-ever” at age 63, we must rule out bleeding/vascular causes urgently. REQUEST TEST: Urgent_Neuro_Imaging (Noncontrast_Head_CT + CTA_Head_Neck if CT negative) and REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP.  

Doctor: While those are arranged, I need to ask one safety question: are you on any blood thinners (warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, clopidogrel, aspirin) or do you have very high blood pressure?
I’m not sure about my blood pressure right now. I don’t take any blood thinners that you listed, and I’m not on aspirin or clopidogrel either.

Doctor: I’m still treating this as a possible vascular/intracranial emergency given the sudden “worst-ever” one-sided temple/forehead/cheek pain at age 63—your next step is immediate imaging: REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW_and_if_negative_CTA_Head_and_Neck_NOW.  
Doctor: While that’s happening, I also need inflammation/giant-cell arteritis screening urgently: REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP_NOW—and check your vitals (including blood pressure).
Okay. I can get the CT and CTA and the ESR/CRP tests. My blood pressure isn’t something I know right now, but I’m willing to have my vitals checked immediately.

Doctor: Good—please get **vitals now** (especially blood pressure) and we will urgently do the ordered **REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW_and_if_negative_CTA_Head_and_Neck_NOW** plus **REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP_NOW**.  

Doctor: While those are arranged, tell me—are you having any scalp tenderness when you comb your hair, any new jaw fatigue with chewing, and did the pain ever come in repeated attacks or is it constant since it started?
No scalp tenderness when I comb my hair, and no new jaw fatigue with chewing. It feels constant since it started—not like repeated attacks.

Doctor: Thanks—so it’s constant severe one-sided facial/temple/forehead pain (not brief attacks), with no scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, or autonomic features, which makes giant-cell arteritis and trigeminal autonomic headache less likely but we must still rule out hemorrhage/vascular causes. REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW_and_if_negative_CTA_Head_and_Neck_NOW, REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP_NOW_and_measured_Vitals_BP.
Understood. I’ll get the CT/CTA and the ESR/CRP as soon as possible, and they should measure my blood pressure and other vitals right now.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since your pain was sudden, severe (“worst-ever”), and started at 63, we must assume a secondary cause until imaging proves otherwise; do you have any of the following right now: confusion, fainting, new trouble speaking, or new weakness/numbness on either side?  
Doctor: If none, the next step is still urgent rule-out—REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW_and_if_negative_CTA_Head_and_Neck_NOW + ESR_and_CRP_NOW_and_current_vitals_including_Blood_Pressure.
No—right now I don’t have confusion, fainting, trouble speaking, or any new weakness or numbness. I’ll get the CT/CTA, ESR/CRP, and my vitals including blood pressure right away.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your sudden “worst-ever” one-sided temple/forehead/cheek pain at age 63 with no neuro deficits or infection symptoms, we must await results to rule out hemorrhage/vascular causes; do you get worse with lying flat, and is there any eye pain or new vision change at all?  
Doctor: While you’re getting your scans and labs, I’m ordering/confirming **REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_NOW_and_if_negative_CTA_Head_and_Neck_NOW + ESR_and_CRP_NOW_and_Blood_Pressure_Vitals**—once results return, I’ll finalize the diagnosis.
No, it doesn’t get worse when I lie flat. And I don’t have eye pain or any new vision change.

Doctor: With no worsening when lying flat, no eye pain, no vision changes, and no neuro deficits, the most important remaining concern is still a secondary cause—so I need your urgent imaging/labs results now (CT/CTA and ESR/CRP) to decide safely.  
Doctor: Please provide the results of **Noncontrast_Head_CT + (if CT negative) CTA_Head_Neck** and **ESR/CRP**; if they’re not back yet, tell me when they’re scheduled.
I don’t have those results yet. The CT/CTA and the ESR/CRP are ordered/scheduled, but I don’t have the timing or the actual numbers right now.

Doctor: I’m going to assume we still haven’t ruled out dangerous secondary causes, so you must go for the scans/labs immediately—REQUEST TEST: STAT_Followup_after_Result_CT/CTA_and_ESR_CRP.  
Doctor: While you’re waiting, do you have any new hearing changes, weakness on one side, trouble finding words, or vomiting—yes or no?
No—I don’t have new hearing changes, one-sided weakness, trouble finding words, or vomiting.

Doctor: Thank you—no hearing change, weakness, speech trouble, or vomiting keeps emergent stroke/ICH less likely but we still can’t rule out vascular or other secondary causes without the imaging and ESR/CRP; have you had the **blood pressure/vitals** checked yet, and did the **STAT CT/CTA** complete?  
Doctor: If results are still pending, please tell me—are you currently having any eye redness, tearing, or new runny nose on the same side as the pain (yes/no)?

I don’t know the blood pressure/vitals result yet, and I’m not sure if the STAT CT/CTA has completed—I’m waiting for the staff to tell me. No, I don’t have eye redness/tearing or new runny nose on the same side as the pain.

Doctor: Thanks—since your STAT CT/CTA and ESR/CRP and vitals are still pending, I can’t safely diagnose a primary headache; the key next step is to immediately review those results and monitor for any new neuro symptoms. Please confirm once you have the CT/CTA report and ESR/CRP numbers, or—if you’re still in the ED—ask staff for a “time completed” for CT/CTA and the current blood pressure reading.
I understand. I’ll confirm as soon as I get the CT/CTA report and the ESR/CRP numbers, and I’ll ask the staff for the “time completed” for the CT/CTA and my current blood pressure reading.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while you’re getting the **CT/CTA time completed**, your **current BP**, and the **ESR/CRP numbers**, I need to decide whether this is still “rule-out emergency” versus a primary headache process; are you currently in the ED or still at home/clinic?  
Doctor: Also, can you tell me whether you have any new symptom since we started—new weakness/numbness, trouble speaking, confusion, fainting, or worsening pain (yes/no)?
I’m in the ED. And no—I haven’t had any new weakness or numbness, trouble speaking, confusion, fainting, or worsening pain since we started.

Doctor: Since you’re in the ED and you have no new neuro symptoms and no worsening, we can wait for the STAT imaging/labs—but you’re still a “rule-out secondary headache” case until CT/CTA and ESR/CRP are back; REQUEST TEST: CT/CTA_Results_Reported_Now_and_ESR_CRP_Numbers_and_Current_BP.  
Doctor: While that’s pending, tell me one last thing: does pressing on the left temple/cheek reproduce or increase the pain (yes/no)?
I don’t have the CT/CTA results or ESR/CRP numbers or my current BP reading yet—I’m waiting for staff to tell me. Pressing on the left temple/cheek does not really reproduce or increase the pain.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your age (63), sudden “worst-ever” one-sided temple/forehead/cheek pain, and still-missing critical results (CT/CTA, ESR/CRP, BP), we must treat this as a secondary headache until proven otherwise. REQUEST TEST: Noncontrast_Head_CT_Result + CTA_Head_Neck_Result + ESR_Result + CRP_Result + Current_BP_Vitals.  
Doctor: If CT/CTA are negative and ESR/CRP and BP are reassuring, the next most likely diagnosis would shift to a neuralgiform/primary headache disorder (though we can’t finalize without those results). DIAGNOSIS READY: Rule-out secondary headache pending CT/CTA and ESR/CRP (temporal arteritis/vascular causes must be excluded).
